title: DataAccessV1dot18
description: K-05 v1.18, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1427: T-320's NEED for the catalog's reads, the lead's ruling DL-888, carded by DL-903; with the architect's rulings on QUESTIONS.md CQ-349 (1) to (4)). It only adds to v1.17 (data-access.v1.17.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to every earlier version down to v1): every v1.17 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none is restated, so every v1 to v1.17 exchange is a v1.18 exchange. Added: five list reads for T-320's catalog and pricing service (actions/src/domain/catalog/reads.ts CatalogReads) and limit 2's owner rules (actions/src/gate/limit-2/facts.ts OwnerRules), each under the call's business scope as rosie_app, on the primary, uncached, in one read-only transaction, answering each row with its id (or, for a row whose primary key is two columns, the name README item 77 gives it) and its version (limit 4): readBusinessKinds (K-23 company_kinds with K-24 kind_flows' combos per flow, and K-23 business_setup.no_money: README item 72), readBusinessServices (K-25 services: item 73), readServiceWays (K-25 service_money: item 74), readServicePriceRules (K-25 price_rules in effect at or after a time, with their conditions, and price_rule_ties: item 75) and readTermsSources (K-23 flow_defaults and the K-26 rules and price_ok_limits in force at a time: item 76). Every column answered is named; never a person's words, number or address, a service's extras or a rule's words. No call, write, state, column, grant, index or migration is added beyond these reads. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

currency.title: CurrencyCode
currency.description: A currency code, three capital letters as ISO 4217 writes them, such as USD (common formats.v1 currency; CQ-09): K-25's service_money.currency and price_rules.currency and K-26's rules.value_currency, as stored. New in v1.18.

catalogFlow.title: CatalogFlow
catalogFlow.description: A flow as K-04 v1 bookings.flow names it and K-23 flow_defaults, K-24 kind_flows, K-25 service_money and K-26 rules and price_ok_limits store it: A, the customer comes to the business (a shop or office, a meeting spot, or video or phone); B, the business goes to the customer (master-A.json, master-B.json). New in v1.18.

spanMinutes.title: SpanMinutes
spanMinutes.description: A span the database holds as an interval (a service's length, a free-cancel time before the visit, a notice) in whole minutes from 1, as T-320's catalog types (actions/src/domain/catalog/types.ts: 'A span ... is whole minutes') and limit 2's RuleRow (actions/src/rules/evaluator/types.ts valueSpanMinutes) read it: the read turns the interval into minutes, extract(epoch from the column) / 60, so a night written as 1 day is 1440 (T-320 default 8). A stored span that is no whole number of minutes, or that counts months, whose length in minutes is not fixed, is never answered rounded or in another form: the call throws and answers nothing (README default 156). K-23, K-25 and K-26 hold every such span above 0 (their CHECKs). New in v1.18.

nullableSpanMinutes.title: NullableSpanMinutes
nullableSpanMinutes.description: A span in whole minutes (spanMinutes), or null where the column is null. New in v1.18.

clockTime.title: ClockTime
clockTime.description: A clock time the database holds as a time (a price rule's from and until; a free-cancel time on the day before the visit) as HH:MM, with :SS only when its seconds are not zero, as K-04's seed fixtures write a time (README item 26) and T-320's catalog reads it ('HH:MM' or 'HH:MM:SS'). A price rule's times are read in the visit's zone, else the business's (K-25 rule 8); a free-cancel time in the business's (K-23 flow_defaults; K-25 service_money). New in v1.18.

nullableClockTime.title: NullableClockTime
nullableClockTime.description: A clock time (clockTime), or null where the column is null. New in v1.18.

nullableCents.title: NullableCents
nullableCents.description: An amount in whole cents above 0, or null where the column is null (CQ-09: integer cents; K-25 service_money_deposit_in_range, service_money_fee_needs_money_before, price_rules_money). New in v1.18.

kindId.title: KindId
kindId.description: A kind of work's id: its profession file's id, such as barber or plumber, or a drafted kind's new-... id (K-23 company_kinds_kind_id_form; K-24 kinds_id_form; K-26 rules_kind_id_form). It holds no slash. New in v1.18.

pluginName.title: PluginName
pluginName.description: A plug-in fact or switch name, lowercase letters and digits (K-23 company_kinds_names_form; SPEC-master 5b, 5d), such as nomoney, sensitive or cancelright. Which names exist is K-26's closed registry (trade_facts, plugin_switches), which no v1.18 read answers: the names come from the compiled bundle and are held to the registry in code (README CQ-349's rulings, (3)). New in v1.18.

moneyPath.title: MoneyPath
moneyPath.description: A money path, price|before|after (SPEC-master 5; K-24 kind_flows_combos_form; K-25 service_money.path), such as list|card|counter: the price from the list, from photos first or at the visit; nothing, a card, a deposit or the full price before; nothing, at the counter (flow A), a bill, the card or the business's own way (flow B) after. Which of the master's 28 a flow allows is K-25's CHECK service_money_path_known and K-24's kind_flows_after_by_flow, not this definition's. New in v1.18.

companyKindRowId.title: CompanyKindRowId
companyKindRowId.description: The name every K-05 row reference gives a K-23 v1 company_kinds row, whose primary key is two columns (company_id, kind_id): the two values in the key's order joined by a slash, <company id>/<kind id>, such as company-lee-home-services/plumber (README item 77; QUESTIONS.md CQ-349 (1)). A kind id holds no slash (company_kinds_kind_id_form), so no two rows share a name. The database builds the name from the row's own columns (company_id || '/' || kind_id), and a commit finds the row by comparing that name with a rowId as a whole, never by splitting the rowId (CQ-09: an id is compared, never parsed). The kind's id alone names no row (refuse-business-kinds-row-by-kind-id). A write names the row by its key, column to value, as K-05 v1 stateWrite's update key says. New in v1.18.

kindFlowRowId.title: KindFlowRowId
kindFlowRowId.description: The name every K-05 row reference gives a K-24 v1 kind_flows row, whose primary key is two columns (kind_id, flow): <kind id>/<flow>, such as plumber/B (README item 77). Built and compared as companyKindRowId says. New in v1.18.

flowDefaultRowId.title: FlowDefaultRowId
flowDefaultRowId.description: The name every K-05 row reference gives a K-23 v1 flow_defaults row, whose primary key is two columns (business_id, flow): <business id>/<flow>, such as biz-lees-barbershop/A (README item 77; CQ-349 (1), the terms snapshot's flow default). A flow is A or B (flow_defaults_flow_known), so no two rows share a name. Built and compared as companyKindRowId says. New in v1.18.

businessSetupRead.title: BusinessSetupRead
businessSetupRead.description: The business's K-23 v1 business_setup row as readBusinessKinds answers it (README item 72; CQ-349 (2)): its no money through Rosie (M02) alone, with the row's key and version, so a way's money path is checked against it (K-25 rule 9: with no money through Rosie, only nothing before and after counter in flow A or own in flow B) and a commit compares that version (limit 4). Never the listing's phone or email, the website, About us, the Stripe account, the terms or control (refuse-business-kinds-setup-listing-phone). New in v1.18.

businessId.description: business_setup.business_id, the row's one-column primary key, so its id in a K-05 row reference (table business_setup).

noMoney.description: business_setup.no_money (FS row M02): true, every service takes nothing up front and is paid the business's own way, and Stripe is not asked.

kindFlowRead.title: KindFlowRead
kindFlowRead.description: A trade's K-24 v1 kind_flows row in one flow, as readBusinessKinds answers it beside its kind (README item 72): the money paths the trade really uses in that flow, the only paths a way of the kind may take there (S1-13; K-25 rule 9), with the row's name and version. Never its main path, switches, arrive or cutoff, which the catalog does not read. New in v1.18.

combos.description: kind_flows.combos, as stored: at least the main path (kind_flows_main_listed).

businessKindRead.title: BusinessKindRead
businessKindRead.description: One of the business's kinds of work, its K-23 v1 company_kinds row, as readBusinessKinds answers it (README item 72), shaped to T-320's BusinessKind (actions/src/domain/catalog/types.ts): its name (companyKindRowId) and key, its own trade name, its facts and the switches on in each flow, its version, and its kind's K-24 kind_flows rows, from which BusinessKind.paths takes each flow's combos (a flow with no row offers no path: a drafted kind not yet reviewed has none). New in v1.18.

businessId.description: company_kinds.business_id, the call's business: a row with another business, or with none, is never answered.

tradeName.description: company_kinds.trade_name, such as Lee Plumbing; null: the business's name.

facts.description: company_kinds.pf_facts, as stored (the nomoney fact among them).

switchesA.description: company_kinds.pf_switches_a: the plug-in switches on in flow A, as stored.

switchesB.description: company_kinds.pf_switches_b: the plug-in switches on in flow B, as stored.

flows.description: The kind's K-24 kind_flows rows, flow A then flow B: two for a trade-file kind, none for a drafted kind (K-24 README 'The flows').

serviceRead.title: ServiceRead
serviceRead.description: A K-25 v1 services row as readBusinessServices answers it (README item 73), shaped to T-320's ServiceRow: its id, business, kind of work, name, price kind, unit, length in whole minutes, place in the list, whether it is offered, and version. Never its extras (what the profession file says, which no code reads by sub-key: refuse-business-services-with-extras). New in v1.18.

name.description: services.name, the business's own word for the line (V01), such as Haircut.

unit.description: services.unit: for per_unit, what one unit is, such as night; null for any other price kind (services_unit_with_per_unit).

position.description: services.position, its place in the list from 1.

wayRead.title: WayRead
wayRead.description: A K-25 v1 service_money row, one way per service and place, as readServiceWays answers it (README item 74), shaped to T-320's WayRow: every column the table has, none of which holds a person's words, number or address. New in v1.18.

locationId.description: service_money.location_id (K-23 locations.id); null only for video.

depositCents.description: service_money.deposit_cents: a set deposit on a deposit path, or null.

depositPercent.description: service_money.deposit_percent: a deposit as a whole percent, 1 to 99, or null.

feeCents.description: service_money.fee_cents: the late-cancel and no-show fee, or null.

currency.description: service_money.currency of the deposit and the fee; null exactly when neither is set.

cutoffBeforeMinutes.description: service_money.cutoff_before in whole minutes: the way's own free-cancel time before the visit, or null.

cutoffDayBeforeAt.description: service_money.cutoff_day_before_at: the way's own free-cancel clock time the day before, or null.

tipLine.description: service_money.tip_line: the way's own tip line, or null (the business's tip_line rule decides).

active.description: service_money.active: offered here for new bookings.

priceConditionsRead.title: PriceConditionsRead
priceConditionsRead.description: A K-25 v1 price rule's conditions (arch 05 line 253: place, worker, time), shaped to T-320's PriceConditions; none set: the service's own price. worker_resource_kind is always worker and is not answered. New in v1.18.

serviceMoneyId.description: price_rules.service_money_id: the place, a way of the same service, or null.

workerResourceId.description: price_rules.worker_resource_id: the worker, a K-04 resources row of kind worker, or null.

weekdays.description: price_rules.weekdays: ISO weekday digits in order, one to six of them, or null for every day (price_rules_weekdays_form).

priceRuleRead.title: PriceRuleRead
priceRuleRead.description: A K-25 v1 price_rules row as readServicePriceRules answers it (README item 75), shaped to T-320's PriceRuleRow: its conditions, price, 'from' price, currency, who set it, its dates and version. effective_to equal to effective_from is a price withdrawn before it started, an empty range that prices no visit. New in v1.18.

fromCents.description: price_rules.from_cents: a visit path's 'from' price, or null.

setByPersonId.description: price_rules.set_by_person_id: who set it (K-04 persons.id), never their name.

priceTieRead.title: PriceTieRead
priceTieRead.description: A K-25 v1 price_rule_ties row as readServicePriceRules answers it (README item 75), shaped to T-320's PriceTieRow: the two rules, when the read-back asked, and the owner's answer once given (until then the lower price applies: S13-25 rule 19). New in v1.18.

flowDefaultRead.title: FlowDefaultRead
flowDefaultRead.description: A K-23 v1 flow_defaults row as readTermsSources answers it (README item 76), shaped to T-320's FlowDefault: the business's default free-cancel time in one flow (H06), exactly one of its two forms set (flow_defaults_one_cutoff), with the row's name (flowDefaultRowId) and version. Never its arrival setting, which the snapshot does not copy. New in v1.18.

cutoffBeforeMinutes.description: flow_defaults.cutoff_before in whole minutes, or null when cutoffDayBeforeAt gives it.

cutoffDayBeforeAt.description: flow_defaults.cutoff_day_before_at, a clock time the day before in the business's zone, or null.

dayRange.title: DayRange
dayRange.description: A K-26 rules.value_dates daterange as limit 2's DayRange reads it (actions/src/rules/evaluator/types.ts): its days in the business's zone, [from, until) in PostgreSQL's canonical form, each YYYY-MM-DD, a null end open. New in v1.18.

ownerRuleRead.title: OwnerRuleRead
ownerRuleRead.description: A K-26 v1 rules row as readTermsSources answers it (README item 76): its kind, value type, scope, typed value, dates and version, which is limit 2's RuleRow (actions/src/rules/evaluator/types.ts) with the version a terms snapshot names it at (T-320's ScopedRow), the kind and the value left unchecked against the registry, as the evaluator checks them. Never the owner's words (rules.words: a note's whole rule, which the AI reads and code never enforces; refuse-terms-sources-rule-with-words) and never who set it. Exactly the value of its type is set, as K-26's CHECK rules_value_matches_type holds every stored row. New in v1.18.

ruleKind.description: rules.rule_kind, a registry kind's name (K-26 rule_kinds.id), such as ok_same_day.

valueType.description: rules.value_type, the kind's one value type (rules_kind_fk).

flow.description: rules.flow, or null for both flows.

kindId.description: rules.kind_id, or null for all the business's kinds of work.

valueOn.description: rules.value_on, set for an on kind alone.

valueCents.description: rules.value_cents, whole cents from 0, set for a money kind alone.

valueSpanMinutes.description: rules.value_span in whole minutes, set for a span kind alone.

valueCount.description: rules.value_count, from 1, set for a count kind alone.

valueDates.description: rules.value_dates, set for a dates kind alone.

priceOkLimitRead.title: PriceOkLimitRead
priceOkLimitRead.description: A K-26 v1 price_ok_limits row as readTermsSources answers it (README item 76), shaped to T-320's ScopedRow: its scope, dates and version, by which a terms snapshot names it (K-30 booking_terms_rules.price_ok_limit_id; K-30 default 11). Not its amounts (quotes, bills, over_cents, currency), which no consumer of v1.18 reads (README open gap 83). New in v1.18.

flow.description: price_ok_limits.flow, or null for both flows.

kindId.description: price_ok_limits.kind_id, or null for all the business's kinds of work.

catalogBusinessNotFoundError.title: CatalogBusinessNotFoundError
catalogBusinessNotFoundError.description: notFound with table businesses: the request's business does not exist, or its own scope does not show it, so a catalog read never answers an empty list under a business that is not there (README items 72 to 76; default 56's rule). Nothing was read beyond the business. New in v1.18.

readBusinessKinds.request.title: ReadBusinessKindsRequest
readBusinessKinds.request.description: The call's business's kinds of work (T-320's CatalogReads.kindsOf): every K-23 company_kinds row of the business, each with its kind's K-24 kind_flows rows, and the business's K-23 business_setup.no_money (README item 72; CQ-349 (2)). The request names one business, the call's own, never null: a business's catalog is that business's, and a null scope would read every business's rows on the runtime side (refuse-business-kinds-no-business). Scope and role: rosie_app on the call's own transaction, rosie.business_id set to the business and confirmed by requireBusinessScope() before the first read. Reads: the primary, uncached, one read-only transaction. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources. New in v1.18.

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (caller.businessId), whose kinds of work are read.

readBusinessKinds.response.title: ReadBusinessKindsResponse
readBusinessKinds.response.description: setup, the business's business_setup row's no_money with its version, or null when the business has no setup row yet, which a consumer reads as not known, never as money allowed (README default 161); kinds, every company_kinds row of the business in (company_id, kind_id) order, compared byte by byte, each with its kind_flows rows, flow A then B; empty when the business has none (README item 72). New in v1.18.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

readBusinessKinds.errors.title: ReadBusinessKindsErrors
readBusinessKinds.errors.description: notFound (table businesses): the business does not exist or its scope does not show it; transient. The binding fails closed on either: a thrown error, never an empty list (README item 72). New in v1.18.

readBusinessServices.request.title: ReadBusinessServicesRequest
readBusinessServices.request.description: The call's business's services (T-320's CatalogReads.servicesOf): every K-25 services row of the business, offered or not (README item 73). The request names one business, the call's own, never null. Scope and role, reads, repeat and time budget as readBusinessKinds. New in v1.18.

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (caller.businessId), whose services are read.

readBusinessServices.response.title: ReadBusinessServicesResponse
readBusinessServices.response.description: services, every services row of the business, offered or not, in (position, id) order, ids compared byte by byte; empty when it has none (README item 73). New in v1.18.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

readBusinessServices.errors.title: ReadBusinessServicesErrors
readBusinessServices.errors.description: As readBusinessKinds.errors (README item 73). New in v1.18.

readServiceWays.request.title: ReadServiceWaysRequest
readServiceWays.request.description: One service's ways (T-320's CatalogReads.waysOf): every K-25 service_money row of the service, offered or not (README item 74). The request names the call's business, never null, and the service. Scope and role, reads, repeat and time budget as readBusinessKinds. New in v1.18.

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (caller.businessId).

serviceId.description: The service whose ways are read (K-25 services.id).

readServiceWays.response.title: ReadServiceWaysResponse
readServiceWays.response.description: ways, every service_money row of the service under the business, offered or not, in id order compared byte by byte; empty for a service with none, for one the scope does not show (another business's) and for one not written yet (built earlier in the same call), never notFound: the caller knows its services from readBusinessServices and its own writes (README item 74, default 153). New in v1.18.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

readServiceWays.errors.title: ReadServiceWaysErrors
readServiceWays.errors.description: As readBusinessKinds.errors: notFound names the business alone, never the service (README item 74). New in v1.18.

readServicePriceRules.request.title: ReadServicePriceRulesRequest
readServicePriceRules.request.description: One service's price rules in effect at or after a time, with their conditions, and its ties (T-320's CatalogReads.priceRulesOf): what a price change closes and what a new rule must not overlap (README item 75). The request names the call's business, never null, the service and the time, a UTC instant ending in Z (refuse-price-rules-at-with-offset). Scope and role, reads, repeat and time budget as readBusinessKinds. New in v1.18.

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (caller.businessId).

serviceId.description: The service whose rules and ties are read (K-25 services.id).

at.description: The instant from which rules are answered: each whose effective_to is null or after it.

readServicePriceRules.response.title: ReadServicePriceRulesResponse
readServicePriceRules.response.description: rules, the service's price_rules rows in effect at or after at (effective_to null or after at; an empty range closed at its own start after at among them), in id order compared byte by byte; ties, every price_rule_ties row of the service, answered or not, in id order. Both empty for a service the scope does not show or not written yet (README item 75, defaults 153 and 157). New in v1.18.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

readServicePriceRules.errors.title: ReadServicePriceRulesErrors
readServicePriceRules.errors.description: As readServiceWays.errors (README item 75). New in v1.18.

readTermsSources.request.title: ReadTermsSourcesRequest
readTermsSources.request.description: A terms snapshot's sources at a time (T-320's CatalogReads.termsSourcesOf) and the business's owner rules (limit 2's OwnerRules.rulesOf): the business's K-23 flow_defaults in both flows, and its K-26 rules and price_ok_limits in force at the time, every scope (README item 76). The request names the call's business, never null, and the time, and no flow: the caller takes its flow's default from the answer (refuse-terms-sources-caller-flow), so one read serves a snapshot and limit 2 alike. Scope and role, reads and repeat as readBusinessKinds. Time budget: none in the sources; inside 'Gate and commit', 300 ms (arch 04 line 223), when limit 2 reads it at the gate. New in v1.18.

businessId.description: The business the call runs under (caller.businessId).

at.description: The instant whose rules and limits are answered: each with tstzrange(effective_from, effective_to, '[)') holding it.

readTermsSources.response.title: ReadTermsSourcesResponse
readTermsSources.response.description: flowDefaults, the business's flow_defaults rows, flow A then B, none for a flow it has no row for; rules and priceOkLimits, its rules and price_ok_limits rows in force at at, of every flow and kind of work, each in id order compared byte by byte: the snapshot keeps those whose scope covers the booking (T-320 terms.ts inForce), and limit 2's evaluator reads every one (README item 76, defaults 158 and 159). New in v1.18.

readAt.description: The database's now() at the read.

readTermsSources.errors.title: ReadTermsSourcesErrors
readTermsSources.errors.description: As readBusinessKinds.errors (README item 76). New in v1.18.
